title: Transfers made soon after an account session begins in an unusual way
definition: Outbound transfers made within a short window of a session that started in an unusual way — a new device, a new location, or a failed authentication followed by a successful one — and that depart from the account's usual transfer pattern. The indicator measures the conjunction of session anomaly and transfer velocity.
evidence_to_cite: the account's historical transfer pattern, over a stated period
benign_explanations: A customer who travels and starts a session from a new device in a new country.
A customer who replaced a phone and is signing in for the first time.
A customer whose password expired and who reset it before a scheduled payment.
A joint account holder who has not used online banking for some time.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, guidance on account takeover and fraud, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.
